podcast.title: Birth and Early Life
podcast.body: Bob Ezrin was born in Toronto in 1949 and grew up as a radio junkie, enjoying pulling in distant American stations with his transistor radio. "He was born in Toronto in 1949 and was a radio junkie growing up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Career Breakthrough
podcast.body: Ezrin's major career breakthrough occurred in the early 1970s when he produced the successful albums for Alice Cooper, subsequently moving on to projects with Lou Reed and Kiss. "His big break came in the early 1970s when he produced the breakthrough albums for Alice Cooper."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Community Involvement
podcast.body: Bob Ezrin is actively involved in community service, serving on numerous boards in Los Angeles, including the Mr. Holland's Opus Foundation and the California Africa American Museum. "He also serves on a ton of community service boards down in Los Angeles, including the Mr. Holland's Opus Foundation and the California Africa American Museum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Continued Musical Passion
podcast.body: Despite his diverse business and community activities, Bob Ezrin remains a fan of music, demonstrating his ongoing involvement by producing Jane's Addiction's reunion album. "It's busy dude, but he's still a fan of music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career and Mentorship
podcast.body: In the 1960s, Bob Ezrin secured a job at a recording studio with Jack Richardson, the producer for The Guess Who. He furthered his education by taking a summer course in music production taught by the legendary producer Phil Ramone. "In the 1960s, Bob got a job working in a recording studio with Jack Richardson, the guest who's producer. He also took a summer course in music production taught by the legendary producer Phil and Ramone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Later Pursuits and Companies
podcast.body: In the 1990s, Bob Ezrin diversified his career by founding Seventh Level Incorporated, an interactive multimedia company responsible for titles like the Monty Python CD-ROM "A Complete Waste of Time" and the children's series "Great Adventure" with Jaime Mandel. He also operates a recording facility called Enigma Digital. "Bob moved on to other pursuits in the 1990s. He founded an interactive multimedia company called Seventh Level Incorporated."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Los Angeles Residency
podcast.body: Bob Ezrin has been living in Los Angeles for several decades. "Bob Ezerman has been a Los Angeles for decades."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Uncle Said's Influence
podcast.body: His uncle, named Said, was a significant music fan who reportedly owned the first stereo system in Canada during the 1950s, when stereo technology was very new. Uncle Said also had a record collection boasting over 15,000 albums. "His uncle said was a big music fan. He apparently had the first ever stereo system in Canada."

xref.title: Evolution to Nimbus School of Recording & Media
xref.body: The studio eventually faced challenges and evolved into the Nimbus School of Recording & Media. It is currently run by Garth Richardson, son of the renowned Canadian producer Jack Richardson, and co-owned by famous Canadian producer Bob Ezrin, known for his work on Pink Floyd's *The Wall* and numerous Kiss records. "Couldn't make it after a while, and eventually evolved into the nimbus school of recording in media, and is run by Garth Richardson, son of the famous Canadian producer Jack Richardson, and is co-owned by Bob Ezren, the famous Canadian producer of Pink Floyd's The Wall, and a ton of kiss records."

xref.title: Mentoring Bob Ezrin
xref.body: Jack Richardson provided Bob Ezrin with his first significant opportunity in a recording studio. "The guy who gave Bob his first proper gig in a recording studio was Jack Richardson, another Toronto guy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Production Philosophy - Collaborative Approach
xref.body: Botrell defines a record producer's responsibility as getting the "best out of the artist and musician and the songs," preferring a collaborative approach over autocratic styles like Todd Rundgren or Bob Ezrin. He encourages artists to try all ideas without argument, quickly discerning what works. "I'm a collaborative producer. So I like to work with the artist."
